title: upgrade attention kernels: flashattnv2 + fused ops + rope/rotary + kv-batching + scheduling
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Motivation: Upgrade the serving runtime's attention kernels to the FlashAttentionV2 variants with selective fused operations and improved rotary/rope handling, plus scheduler-level changes and KV cache batching to reduce end-to-end latency and unit cost for long-context workloads. This PR combines multiple coordinated changes that were previously landed in isolation to produce measurable improvements in throughput and memory usage for production workloads.

Summary of changes (single PR combining kernel + runtime changes):
- Integrate FlashAttentionV2 kernels behind a runtime feature-flag and a targetable kernel selector. The selector prefers fused-kernel variants for eligible QKV shapes and falls back to the legacy path on unsupported tensors.
- Add fused ops for qkv projection + dropout + bias-add for specific model layouts to reduce kernel launch overhead.
- Improve rotary/rope support: unified rotary embedding application with fused rotation + attention matmul when sequence length >= 512 to reduce memcopy and extra kernels.
- KV cache batching: introduce continuous-batching-aware KV packing that coalesces multiple small KV updates into a single batched kernel for multi-request steady state. Works with pinned dedicated pools and hosted autoscale.
- Scheduling: extend the request scheduler to prefer batched KV flush windows and introduce a short-execution-path for low-latency single-token requests. Adds heuristics to avoid reordering for strict token ordering use-cases.
- Runtime configuration: new flags --attn-kernel=auto|flashv2|legacy, --kv-batch-window-ms, and --rotary-threshold tokens. Defaults preserve current behavior (auto).
- Tests/bench: microbenchmarks for a spectrum of seq-len and batch-size shapes; end-to-end benchmarks using real production prompt distributions.

Commits and rationale: see commits list for granular changes. The PR attempts to keep backward compatibility: falling back to legacy kernels when GPU/driver/kernel unsupported and exposing opt-in flags for early rollouts.

Checklist:
- [x] Kernel integration and kernel selector
- [x] Fused op kernels + CPU fallback implementations
- [x] Scheduler heuristics + KV-batching logic + config knobs
- [x] Unit tests for rotary and fused op codepaths
- [x] E2E perf harness and benchmark results included
- [x] Docs update stub (console config page)

Impact and rollout plan: This is safe to rollout behind the default "auto" selector. We will enable FlashAttentionV2 by default on dedicated pools after canarying on 10% of traffic in the next sprint. If any regression is detected, the runtime will fall back to legacy kernels and we will hotfix.

Notes on potential risks: driver bugs on older CUDA versions; larger temporary GPU memory usage for certain fused kernels in extreme sequence-length cases (mitigated by rotary-threshold and attn-kernel config).

Tested against: NVIDIA driver 535.x, 540.x; CUDA 11.8/12.1; ROCm not supported in this patch (fallback to legacy).

References: ENG-3104 (kernel perf initiative), ENG-3112 (kv-cache batching), previous PRs that introduced incremental kernel upgrades.

release_notes: Performance: Upgrades attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 with fused QKV ops and improved rotary/rope handling. Adds KV-batching and scheduler heuristics to reduce latency and cost for long-context workloads. Backwards compatible via runtime selector and config flags.
benchmarks: baseline (legacy): GPT-like model, seq_len=1024, batch=8 => p50 latency 48ms, throughput 195 tok/s
patch (flashv2+fused): same config => p50 latency 36ms (-25%), throughput 255 tok/s (+31%)
longseq (seq_len=4096, batch=1): baseline p50 420ms, patch p50 310ms (-26%)
kv-batching steady-state: small-request mix throughput +18% and 12% CPU/GPU kernel reduction
testing: unit: new tests for kernel selector, fused qkv op, rotary correctness
integration: KV cache packing validated against existing cache semantics
e2e: perf harness runs across production prompt distributions, canary on 10% traffic
regression: run against pre-existing attn regression test-suite; no functional regressions observed
